purpose: Source-supported expert discovery, not clinical credential assessment, current availability or clinical superiority.

grades.3: Direct source evidence supports the central requested expertise and all explicitly essential requested criteria. The evidence category must match the request: an interest is enough for an interest request, not for performed activity. Historical evidence is sufficient only if the request does not demand current activity.
grades.2: Direct source evidence supports the central expertise, with clearly identifiable unconfirmed secondary or essential requirements. The candidate is useful to investigate, not represented as fully qualified.
grades.1: Adjacent topic or professional background only; direct evidence for the central request is absent. It may be honestly displayed as indirect, but is not counted as a useful answer to that request.
grades.0: No relevant owned evidence, documented incompatible central role/expertise, wrong-person attribution, or only an unsupported inference.
grades.null: Not yet judged, disputed attribution/meaning, or insufficient review material. Never counted as irrelevant. Blocks scored-pool completion.

metrics.usefulPrecisionAt5: Grade >=2, divided by the first min(5, returned candidates). Empty answerable rankings score 0. Report result count and useful coverage at five separately to expose underfilling; a run must not omit useful pool candidates while reporting a perfect one-result precision.
metrics.usefulCoverageAt5: Useful candidates returned in first five / min(5, useful candidates in the complete judged pool). Zero when the judged pool has useful candidates but the run returns none; null only for no useful pool candidate.
metrics.ndcgAt10: DCG using gain 2^grade-1 and log2(rank+1), divided by the ideal ranking in the same completely judged union pool. Pool-relative, not exhaustive corpus relevance. Null when no positive graded candidate exists; report separately as insufficient evidence.
metrics.knownRecallAt20: Only for bounded scenarios with independently accepted source-reviewed anchors. Missing or held anchors remain visible; no automatic denominator removal. Broad scenarios have no corpus-recall claim.
metrics.aggregation: Macro average per brief, then by family. Report paired baseline differences, denominators and deterministic brief-level bootstrap intervals. Unknown judgements or incomplete top-ten judgements invalidate metrics rather than being filled with zeros.

review.pool: Union top 20 from BM25, semantic and hybrid for every release plus frozen source anchors; deduplicate identical candidate evidence fingerprints. Every scored top ten and every ideal-pool item must have a resolved dual review before final metrics.
review.disagreement: Keep both independent judgements. A third source-based adjudication records the chosen grade and reason; unresolved meaning or attribution blocks that item. Never average conflicting grades into an accepted claim.
review.minimumRationale: State why the central request is or is not supported, name the supporting evidence tokens, distinguish interests from activity, and enumerate material requested gaps.

holdout.access: Runner and independent reviewers only; ranking implementer receives development cases and aggregate held-out gates, not held-out labels before the implementation is frozen.
holdout.contamination: If a held-out failure is disclosed for development, mark that case consumed, preserve the first report, and create a fresh sealed confirmation set before signoff.

invariants: Never grade a candidate by regex alone.
Never infer present practice from ingestion timestamps.
Never infer independence or regulatory approval from missing fields.
Never turn unknown essential requirements into confirmed support.
Never count interests, training or language proficiency as performed clinical activity.
Never silently rewrite the original 98 cases.
No external model calls are made by this harness.
